close_reason: Cannot eliminate the manual Serialize/Deserialize/Display triplication — workspace dep policy in crate AGENTS.md forbids strum and serde_with. The bead's own analysis acknowledged this constraint. Actionable fix: replaced the single-variant 'Singleton round-trips' test (1 of 23 typed variants audited) with a table-driven test that iterates ALL 23 typed variants and asserts (a) Display produces the expected wire string, (b) Serialize emits the same, (c) Deserialize rebuilds the typed variant — explicitly NOT Custom. A future contributor that adds a Display arm without a matching Deserialize arm now fails (c) at first test run, catching the silent drift filed as bd:JMAP-wlip.22 mechanically. The triplication maintenance burden remains; it's now testable. Resolves the unaudited-synchronization risk without changing the dep allowlist.
description: src/backend.rs:244-321 implements three parallel mappings for SetErrorType's 24 known variants plus the Custom(String) catch-all: (1) Display (lines 246-272) maps each variant to its camelCase wire string; (2) Serialize (276-280) delegates to to_string(); (3) Deserialize (282-320) hand-writes a Visitor with a 24-arm match that mirrors Display in reverse. Adding a variant requires touching exactly two arms (Display and Deserialize). The pairs MUST stay in sync — a Display string like 'overQuota' that doesn't appear in the Deserialize match becomes a Custom('overQuota') on round-trip, producing the silent contract drift already filed as JMAP-wlip.22. Idiomatic Rust uses #[serde(rename_all = 'camelCase')] + #[serde(untagged)] (or a Custom variant with serde(other)) to derive the round-trip from a single source of truth, OR uses strum::Display/EnumString to derive Display alongside FromStr. The workspace dep policy in crate AGENTS.md restricts deps to 'serde, serde_json, tokio, http, thiserror' — neither strum nor serde_with is on the list. That makes the manual impl a forced choice today, but the choice is not a free maintenance lunch: the 24-arm pair is the same maintenance burden the policy was trying to avoid, and JMAP-wlip.22's round-trip asymmetry is exactly the failure mode this section warns about. What goes wrong if it stays: every future RFC extension that adds a typed variant requires synchronized edits to Display + Deserialize arms; the test asserting 'Singleton round-trips as singleton' (line 919) covers exactly one variant out of 24, so the synchronization is unaudited for 23 of them.
title: SetErrorType manual Serialize/Deserialize + Display triplicates the variant→wire-string mapping
